svg.title: A learned period-3 positional clock in SpliceBERT
svg.text: A learned period-3 positional clock drives codon reading and splice-site pairing in SpliceBERT
The clock is stored in the position-embedding table, read out by six attention heads, and required for both coding prediction and the donor–acceptor circuit.
The clock is in the position table
Fourier power of P [1026 × 512] along the position axis, relative to the median bin
the next-shortest strong mode has period 10.7 — period 3 stands alone
13× more mod-3 structure than the human-only model
Six heads read the clock — and it is a period-3 sawtooth
R(k) = mean_i (W_Q·h_i)·(W_K·h_{i+k}), centred. Computed from the weights and the position-conditional residual stream — no sequence content.
period-3 clock deleted from P (7 of 513 Fourier bins)
Delete the clock → attention collapses to chance
dominant phase mass of each head's local attention (empirical, post-softmax). Control = an energy-matched Fourier band.
Delete the clock → coding prediction and the splicing circuit die
% of intact retained, as the clock is attenuated by α
α — clock amplitude retained in P (1 = intact, 0 = deleted)
dashed = energy-matched control band removed instead (nothing happens)

The clock is a rank-2 rotary phase code at period 3, learned in stage-1 pretraining and only with multi-species data. Deleting it costs 0.159 nats of masked-base log-prob in coding exons vs 0.042 in introns

(21 energy-matched control bands: 0.029 / 0.031 — equal; add-one p = 0.046), and destroys the donor–acceptor coupling (0.946 → 0.027). Restoring L2H15 alone recovers 36% of it (24 random single heads: 0.7% mean, 4.2% max; p = 0.040).
